questions.q: Why does the Average Order Value calculated field use COUNTD([Sales Order Id]) instead of a plain row count?
options: COUNTD is required syntax for all Tableau calculated fields
The underlying data is at the order-line grain, so a plain row count would count lines, not distinct orders
COUNTD is the only function that can divide two numbers in Tableau
Sales Order Id cannot be counted any other way
questions.explain: This mirrors exactly why the Power BI measure used DISTINCTCOUNT — counting distinct order IDs is what actually answers 'how many orders' from a line-grain fact table.

questions.q: What makes {FIXED : SUM([Line Total])} behave like Power BI's CALCULATE + ALL(DimTerritory) pattern?
options: Both functions sort the data before aggregating
Naming no dimensions inside FIXED computes one single, constant value regardless of the view's current filters, the same way ALL strips away filters
FIXED only works when connected to SQL Server specifically
They produce different results and are not actually equivalent
questions.explain: An LOD expression with no dimensions named inside FIXED ignores the view's current filter context, producing a genuinely constant company-wide number — the direct analog of ALL in DAX.

questions.q: Why is FIXED the correct LOD keyword here, rather than INCLUDE or EXCLUDE?
options: INCLUDE and EXCLUDE are deprecated in current Tableau versions
INCLUDE and EXCLUDE both adjust detail relative to the view's current dimensions, so their result can still change with the view; FIXED with no dimensions named produces a truly constant value
FIXED is the only LOD keyword that supports SUM as its aggregation
There is no functional difference between the three keywords
questions.explain: A board-wide benchmark needs a value that never changes regardless of what's on the sheet — only FIXED with no dimensions named guarantees that.

questions.q: What does a Tableau dashboard action (Filter type) accomplish when added between two worksheets?
options: It permanently deletes data from one worksheet
Clicking a mark in one worksheet filters the other, giving the Board the same kind of click-through interactivity Executives got in Power BI
It exports both worksheets to PDF automatically
It merges the two worksheets into a single calculated field
questions.explain: A filter action is Tableau's native mechanism for linking worksheets so a selection in one drives what's shown in another.

questions.q: What is Pct of Company Total built from in this lesson, and what pattern does it mirror?
options: SUM([Line Total]) divided by [Total Sales (All Territories)] — the same benchmark-and-share pattern built in DAX back in Lesson 12
A hardcoded percentage with no relationship to the FIXED LOD expression
COUNTD([Sales Order Id]) divided by the total row count
It has no equivalent anywhere else in this capstone
questions.explain: This recreates the exact benchmark-and-share logic from Power BI's Pct of Company Total measure, using Tableau's own calculated field syntax on top of the FIXED LOD expression.
